guideTitle: 6 Best Transfer Benches With Commode Openings in 2026
metaTitle: Best Transfer Benches With Commode Cutouts
metaDescription: Six transfer benches with a commode or hygiene cutout compared by slide, pail setup, seat size and weight rating, from toilet-to-tub sliders to padded combos.
introParagraphs: A cutout in a transfer bench seat does one of two jobs. In some products it is a hygiene opening that gives access for personal washing while the user sits on a bath bench. In others it is a full commode opening, with a pail, lid and splash guard, so the same piece of equipment works as a bedside toilet and as a tub bench. They look similar in photographs and are very different in use, so the first question is which job you need done.

The six picks here cover both. The two Eagle Health Supplies benches slide and, in the case of the 77963 model, connect the toilet to the tub across a 29.5-inch slide. The Platinum Health HydroGlyde is a padded 420 lb slider with a snap-in cutout insert, the Medline with a bucket is a straightforward fixed bench, and the Drive Medical and Medline Padded combination benches add a cushioned commode seat.

We evaluated each from listing specs and buyer feedback, not from hands-on lab work. For anything that doubles as a commode, cleaning and hygiene are part of the design problem, so we look at how each cutout is covered, what comes in the box and how easy the parts are to wash.

products.name: Eagle Health Supplies Toilet-to-Tub Transfer Bench with Cut Out Seat, 77963
products.description:
The Eagle 77963 combines a sliding shower transfer bench with an extra-wide commode seat so a user can move sideways between the toilet and the tub without standing. The listing gives a sliding distance of 29.5 inches, a seat of 20.25 by 18.5 inches, overall dimensions of 55.5 by 22.5 by 37.75 inches and a maximum tub clearance of 19 inches, with a seat height from the floor of 20.25 to 24.25 inches.

That design only works when the toilet and the tub sit next to each other, which is common in smaller bathrooms but not universal. The reinforced aluminum frame carries 350 lb, a safety belt secures the user and adjustable-height legs with rubber tips grip the floor. It is 100 percent reversible, sets up in under 5 minutes without tools and is FSA and HSA eligible.

It sits in the upper half of the price range. Compared with the fixed benches it moves the user the full distance without a stand. Choose it when the toilet and tub are side by side and standing is difficult. Before ordering, measure the line from the toilet seat position to the tub edge, and leave a helper's standing room on the open side. Wipe the cutout seat and rails dry after use, and keep the slide track free of soap film.
products.bestFor: Bathrooms where the toilet and tub are side by side and standing is hard.
pros: 29.5 inch slide between toilet and tub
FSA and HSA eligible per the listing
cons: 55.5 inch overall width needs a lot of room

products.name: Eagle Health Supplies Toilet-to-Tub Transfer Bench with Cut Out Seat, 77993
specs: Seat slides and locks at each end
products.description:
The 77993 is the second Eagle toilet-to-tub model, with a cutout seat that allows for personal cleaning and bathing at home or in an assisted living facility. The listing describes a seat that slides and locks at each end, tool-free assembly and a height-adjustable frame, and says the bench lets the user go from the toilet to the bathtub with less risk of falling during transfers.

The listing gives fewer numbers than the 77963 in the material we reviewed, so check the product page for the weight rating, slide length and overall dimensions before ordering. It also warns that this hygiene product is non-returnable once opened, and asks the buyer to measure the tub and bathroom carefully.

It sits in the upper-middle of the price range. Compared with the 77963 it is described more briefly but shares the slide-and-lock concept. Choose it after confirming the numbers and the fit. Because the product page is the only place to find the weight rating and slide length in the material we reviewed, read it before ordering. Practice the slide and the end locks with a helper, and wipe the cutout seat dry after each use. Compared with the 77963 it asks you to do more of your own checking, and the non-returnable policy makes that homework worth doing.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a cutout slide bench and will verify the dimensions first.
pros: Seat slides and locks at each end
cons: Few numbers in the material we reviewed

products.name: Platinum Health HydroGlyde Sliding Padded Transfer Bench with Cut Out Seat
products.description:
The HydroGlyde is a premium padded sliding bench with a seat cutout and a snap-in insert that can be added or removed as desired, with a mounting bracket keeping the insert within arm's reach. The aluminum frame is described as institutional quality and rust-proof, with a stated 420 lb capacity, an overall height of 30 to 35 inches and a frame length of 38 inches.

The insert makes the cutout optional: you can leave it in for ordinary bathing and take it out when hygiene access is needed. The padding is warm to the touch compared with hard plastic, and the sliding design eliminates the shuffle across a fixed bench. The Hi-View gray color is meant to stand out against a white bathroom for users with poor vision.

It sits near the top of the price range. Compared with the Eagle benches it adds padding and a snap-in insert. Choose it for a padded slider with a removable cutout. Seat the insert firmly each time, clean the cutout edges with a mild cleaner and dry the padding after use. Practice the slide and rotation with a helper, and keep the mounting bracket within reach.
products.bestFor: Users who want a padded slider with a removable cutout insert.
pros: Snap-in cutout insert with a bracket
cons: Costs near the top of the range

products.name: Medline Transfer Bench with Perineal Cutout and Bucket, 400 lb
products.description:
The Medline is the straightforward fixed bench with a commode cutout. It comes with a pail, a lid and a splash guard, a 400 lb weight capacity, a seat height of 18 to 22 inches and a seat depth of 16 inches. The listing is short and plain.

Because it is a fixed bench, the user shuffles across it rather than being slid, which suits people who can move themselves. The pail and lid let the bench serve as a commode when the bathroom is far away, and the cutout allows for hygiene access in the tub. The listing publishes few other dimensions in the material we reviewed.

It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the Eagle slide benches it is simpler and less expensive but does not span the toilet and tub. Choose it for a fixed bench that doubles as a commode. Wash the pail, lid and splash guard separately from the frame, and store the pail covered when it is not needed. Wipe the seat dry and check the suction cups before each bath.
products.bestFor: Users who can shuffle and need a bench that doubles as a commode.
pros: Pail, lid and splash guard included

products.name: Medline Padded Combination Transfer Bench and Commode, 400 lb
products.description:
This Medline adds padding and a side arm to the combination concept. It has a commode cutout, a side arm for secure transfers, suction cup feet and a 400 lb capacity, with an adjustable seat height of 18 to 22 inches and a seat depth of 16 inches. A pail, a lid and a splash guard come with it, and it ships without retail packaging to reduce waste.

The padding makes the seat more comfortable for longer sits, which matters when the bench is doubling as a commode. The side arm gives the user something to push on. The same cleaning issues apply as for any commode: the pail and lid need washing and the padding needs wiping.

It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the plain Medline with a bucket it adds padding and an arm. Choose it for a padded, armed combination bench. Clean the pail and lid after each use, wipe the padded seat and arm with a mild cleaner and let them dry. Check that the suction cups hold on the tub floor.
products.bestFor: Users who want padding and an arm on a combination bench.
pros: Padded seat with a side arm
Pail, lid and splash guard included
cons: Few dimensions beyond seat height and depth

products.name: Drive Medical Transfer Bench Commode Chair for Toilet
products.description:
Drive Medical's 2-in-1 design combines a transfer bench and a commode, with dual-column extension legs for height adjustment from 18 to 22.5 inches, a cushioned seat and backrest and a 1-inch aluminum frame. The seat is 24 by 16 inches, the width between the arms is 18 inches and the overall dimensions are 17.25 by 28.5 by 30 inches. The backrest adjusts without tools and extra-large suction cups add stability.

The published width between the arms is useful, because it tells you whether the user will fit comfortably. The cushioned seat and backrest are warmer than bare plastic. The listing describes it as a comfortable, portable toilet and an adjustable bedside commode, so it is used as a commode first and a transfer bench second.

It sits in the lower-middle of the price range. Compared with the Medline combination it publishes more dimensions. Choose it for a cushioned commode bench with clear measurements. Set the arm spacing check against the user's hips before you decide, and adjust the seat back without tools. Wipe the cushion and the suction cups after use.
products.bestFor: Users who want a cushioned commode bench with published arm spacing.
cons: Designed more as a commode than a tub bench

buyingCriteria.explanation: A cutout with a snap-in insert, as on the HydroGlyde, gives hygiene access during bathing. A commode opening with a pail, lid and splash guard, as on both Medline benches and the Drive Medical, lets the bench serve as a toilet. The Eagle benches use cutout seats for cleaning and toilet-to-tub movement. Decide which job the cutout must do before you compare anything else. If you will use the bench as a commode at night, look for a pail you can empty easily.

The Eagle 77963 slides 29.5 inches, enough to span from the toilet to the tub, but it needs about 55.5 inches of width. A bench like this only works if the toilet and tub sit side by side. Measure the distance from the toilet to the tub edge and compare it with the slide. If your layout is different, a fixed combination bench is the better choice. Draw the room with the toilet, the tub and the clearances before choosing a slider.

The Eagle 77963 seat is 20.25 by 18.5 inches, the Drive Medical's is 24 by 16 with 18 inches between the arms and the Medline's depth is 16 inches. A larger seat suits a larger user, and a published arm gap tells you whether hips will fit. Check these numbers against the user's measurements. Measure the user's hip width while seated and compare it to the arm gap.

The Medline benches include a pail, a lid and a splash guard. The HydroGlyde includes a snap-in insert with a mounting bracket. The Eagle benches rely on the cutout only. Count what you need: a bench without a pail cannot be used as a commode. Confirm the contents before you order. Ask what is in the box if a listing is short.

A padded commode seat is more comfortable but needs wiping and drying, and the pail and lid need regular washing. The HydroGlyde and padded Medline have cushioned seats, while the plain Medline and Eagle benches are firmer. Choose surfaces that you will actually clean, and keep a cleaning routine in place. If a caregiver does the cleaning, choose the design with the fewest crevices.

Ratings are 420 lb on the HydroGlyde, 400 lb on both Medline benches and the Drive Medical, and 350 lb on the Eagle 77963, with the Eagle 77993 not stating one in the material we reviewed. The 77993 listing warns the product is non-returnable once opened, so measure first. A rating is a ceiling, so leave margin. A non-returnable policy is a reason to double-check every number you can.

howWeEvaluated.title: Which cutout job it does
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated hygiene cutouts on the Eagle and HydroGlyde from full commode setups on the two Medline benches and the Drive Medical. Each suits a different need. A cutout that does the wrong job is no use, however good the bench.

howWeEvaluated.title: Slide and layout
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the 29.5 inch slide on the Eagle 77963 with the lock-at-each-end slide on the 77993 and the HydroGlyde's frame length of 38 inches. A slide is only an advantage if the layout allows. A slide that cannot fit the room is a drawback, not a feature.

howWeEvaluated.title: Seat room
howWeEvaluated.description: We read seat sizes and arm gaps, including the Drive Medical's 24 by 16 inches and 18 inch arm spacing and the Eagle's 20.25 by 18.5 inch seat. Published arm gaps made it easier to judge fit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Inclusions and hygiene
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited pails, lids and splash guards, the HydroGlyde's snap-in insert and wipe-clean surfaces. We noted what a buyer must supply. Contents lists were treated as part of the product.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and fit clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: We recorded ratings and flagged missing numbers and the non-returnable policy on the 77993. A missing rating and a non-returnable policy together raise the stakes for checking.

faq.q: What is the difference between a cutout and a commode opening?
faq.a: A hygiene cutout gives access for personal washing on a bath bench, while a commode opening has a pail, lid and splash guard so the bench works as a toilet. Some benches offer both. Decide which you need before ordering.

faq.q: Will a toilet-to-tub bench fit my bathroom?
faq.a: Only if the toilet and tub are side by side and there is room for the width. The Eagle 77963 is 55.5 inches wide and slides 29.5 inches. Measure the distance and the clear floor, and consider a fixed bench if the layout does not suit.

faq.q: How do I clean the pail and lid?
faq.a: Empty and rinse the pail after each use, wash it with a household disinfectant and dry it. Wipe the lid and splash guard, and keep the commode out of the bath area when it is not in use. Wash your hands afterward.

faq.q: Can the cutout insert stay in?
faq.a: On the HydroGlyde, yes. The snap-in insert can be left in for ordinary bathing and removed when needed, and a bracket keeps it within reach. Check that it is seated before use.

faq.q: Can I return a hygiene bench?
faq.a: Often not. The Eagle 77993 listing says it is non-returnable once opened. Measure your tub and bathroom carefully, and confirm the numbers on the product page before opening the box.
For sliding benches, yes, at least at first. A helper guides the seat and watches for slipping. Fixed combination benches can be used independently if the user can shuffle.

faq.q: Is it safe to use a transfer bench as a commode?
faq.a: Only the benches designed for it, with a pail, lid and splash guard, such as the two Medline benches and the Drive Medical. Do not improvise a commode from an ordinary bench. Keep the pail secure, clean it after each use and check that the seat and legs are stable before every sit.
